title: Multivariable Limits Fail Along Different Paths
topic: A two-variable limit must agree no matter how you approach the point. For f(x, y) = (x y + y³) / (x² + y²), approaching the origin along the x-axis gives zero; approaching along y equals x gives one half. Two different values, so the limit does not exist.
concepts: limit of a function of two variables

beats.narration: In one variable, a limit just has to agree from the left and from the right. In two variables, every direction has a vote.

elements.content: Hook caption: every path has a vote.

beats.narration: Consider f of x comma y, equal to x y plus y cubed, divided by x squared plus y squared. The denominator goes to zero at the origin. Does f have a limit there?
Walk in along the x-axis. Set y to zero. Then f reduces to x times zero plus zero, divided by x squared. That is zero. The limit along this path is zero.

elements.content: Path arrow along x-axis toward origin in violet

beats.narration: Now walk in along the diagonal where y equals x. Substitute: the numerator becomes x squared plus x cubed; the denominator is two x squared. As x goes to zero, the ratio approaches one half. The limit along this path is one half.

elements.content: Path arrow along y = x toward origin in amber

beats.narration: Two different answers along two different paths. So the two variable limit at the origin does not exist.
